# Survey Graphs {#sec-graphs-survey}

The graphs in this chapter are available from the `r keys("Survey")` button in the **Graphs** section of the **Analyses** tab.
Along with the options described here, each graph's editor includes the [shared pages](#sec-editor-common) (e.g., **Axes**, **Legend**, and **Placement**).

## Likert Chart {#sec-likert-dlg}

A Likert chart shows how respondents answered survey questions on an agreement scale.
The responses are drawn as bars diverging from the neutral point into negative and positive responses.
The dataset should have one row per respondent, with a column for each question holding that respondent's answer coded as a whole number.

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
Import the question columns as integers, and leave the missing data code as 0.
Then, assign a label to each response value so that the legend can describe them.
:::

### Variables {-}

**Questions**: The survey questions, each one a column of responses.
Every question must use the same scale, and the number of points in that scale is deduced from the responses.
The responses are coded as follows:

- **0**: No response (a missing value is also counted as no response).
- **1**: The most negative response.
- **2** and up: The responses in between, up to the most positive one.

Select the questions in the order that they should appear.

**Group** (optional): Splits each question's responses into one bar per group (e.g., by gender).

### Options {-}

**Show response counts**: Check this option to show the number of responses next to each question.

**Show percentages**: Check this option to show the percentages on the bars.

**Show section headers**: Check this option to show headers above the response sections (e.g., *Positive* above the positive responses).

**Adjust bar widths to respondent size**: Check this option to make each bar's width reflect its number of respondents.

**Negative color**: Select the color of the negative responses.

**Positive color**: Select the color of the positive responses.

**Neutral color**: Select the color of the neutral responses.

**No-response color**: Select the color of the responses with no answer.

**Positive label**: Enter the header for the positive responses.

**Negative label**: Enter the header for the negative responses.

**No-response label**: Enter the header for the responses with no answer.

**Question brackets**: Add brackets to title a range of related questions.
Each bracket has a **Title**, a **Start question**, and an **End question**.

\newpage

## Word Cloud {#sec-word-cloud-dlg}

A word cloud shows words sized by how often they occur, so that the most common ones stand out.
The dataset should have a column of words, either with one row per occurrence or one row per word with a column of its frequency.

### Variables {-}

**Word**: The words to display.
If no weight column is used, then each word is sized by how many times it appears.

**Weight** (optional): The frequency count of the word in the same row.
Use this when the words have already been tallied.

### Options {-}

**Minimum frequency**: Enter the lowest frequency that a word must have to be included.
This is useful for leaving out rare words.

**Maximum frequency**: Enter the highest frequency that a word can have to be included.
This is useful for leaving out very common words.

**Maximum words**: Enter the maximum number of words to show.
Only the most frequent words are included.

\newpage

## Pro & Con Roadmap {#sec-procon-roadmap-dlg}

A pro & con roadmap shows positive and negative sentiments as stops along a road, sized by how often each one was mentioned or by its total.
The dataset should have one column of positive sentiments and one column of negative sentiments.
Each can be paired with a column of totals; otherwise, the labels are counted.

### Variables {-}

**Positive (pros)**: The positive sentiments (e.g., strengths or advantages).
Repeated labels are counted by frequency unless a values column is provided.

**Positive values** (optional): Pre-calculated totals for each positive sentiment, used instead of counting how often it appears.

**Negative (cons)**: The negative sentiments (e.g., weaknesses or drawbacks).
Repeated labels are counted by frequency, unless a values column is provided.

**Negative values** (optional): Pre-calculated totals for each negative sentiment, used instead of counting how often it appears.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The positive and negative columns do not need to line up row by row, as each column is aggregated on its own.
If the same label appears in both columns, then only its net total is shown, on the side with the larger count.
Labels that cancel out are left off.
:::

### Options {-}

**Minimum count**: Enter the lowest count (or total) that a sentiment must have to be included.

**Positive label**: Enter the label describing the positive sentiments.

**Negative label**: Enter the label describing the negative sentiments.

**Marker labels**: Select how each stop is labeled (**Name only**, **Name and value**, or **Name and absolute value**).

**Road color**: Select the color of the road.

**Lane separator**: Select how the road's lanes are separated (**Single line**, **Double line**, or **None**).

**Road stop theme**: Select how the stops are drawn (**Location markers** or **Road signs**).

**Add explanatory caption**: Check this option to add a caption explaining how to read the roadmap.
